plan.metric: dollars spent within two weeks of the e-mail
plan.power_note: Give the smallest change in the average worth detecting and how much the amount varies to see the power of this test.
plan.expectation: Retrospective replay of a public randomised e-mail test; no expectation was set in advance.

plan_preview.basis: A two-sided comparison of the average amount of the contacted and the held-back customers at 95% confidence, and a chance of 80% of seeing a change of the size shown, up or down. The spread of the amount is the one in the test plan. The test plan's earlier amount is expected to explain 0.02% of the spread, and the adjusted comparison removes that much of it. The cost of holding customers back assumes the campaign changes each customer's amount by exactly the size shown, valued at what one unit is worth; contacting customers outside the selection costs every contact, plus the offer for those who take it. Every number is worked out from the counts entered; no customer data is used.

report.summary: Contacted customers averaged 1.39 against 0.55 for the control group: a difference of +0.84 per customer (95% CI +0.23 to +1.45; p = 0.007), about 3,578 more in total across the contacted customers. Taking account of each customer's 'history' from before the campaign, the difference is +0.84 per customer (95% CI +0.23 to +1.45); this removed 0% of the chance variation. A few very large amounts dominate these averages, so the range may be too narrow; more customers in each group would make it reliable.

verdict.detail: Likely between 984 and 6,178 in total (+0.84 per contacted customer). Adjusted for each customer's 'history' before the campaign.
